title: Signal Processing UI
tagline: A web app that lets researchers run each other's signal-processing scripts straight from the browser — no installs, no setup.
summary: A single web interface that lets the research team use each other's signal-processing scripts without installing anything or untangling someone else's code.
overview: In research, “don't reinvent the wheel” is the rule — especially with signal-processing code, which is intricate and hard to follow from the outside. Actually reusing it, though, is easier said than done.

Before this project, team members shared code as .zip files over Teams or by cloning and forking GitHub repos, and then had to get it running on their own machines — which often caused more problems than it solved.
I built one website where anyone on the team can run a colleague's scripts through a simple form and see the results, without dealing with installation or the code itself.
I developed it as a part-time job during my third year of studies and presented it at the IEEC Forum. It also opened the door to more responsibility on later projects.
